recommendation: Keep the no-change audit commit. No core source follow-up is needed for FHIR-5505 unless a future reconciliation elects to audit merged comment FHIR-5454 independently.
issue_request: FHIR-5505 was a Published/Persuasive with Modification OO change request from the January 2015 DSTU1 ballot. It asked the Device UDI notes to explain DI/PI components, treat UDI as a global concept with jurisdictional repositories, use US GUDID as a local example, and require Device details to be consistent with the UDI string or local repository rather than only GUDID.
initial_application: Commit 85cad2a017a228c70b358dab887c56b5bfccb18e pre-applied FHIR-5505 together with related Device ballot comments before the 2015-03-26 OO block vote. Its Device notes patch changed the old GUDID-only consistency wording to jurisdictional repository/local repository language and moved the US GUDID text into an example.
additional_context: Device is active in the current build. The current source has evolved from the old DSTU1 Device.udi string to Device.udiCarrier, but source/device/device-notes.xml still carries the approved FHIR-5505 concepts: IMDRF/UDI background, FDA/GUDID as a US example, DI/PI/other UDI elements, jurisdictional repository storage, and local-repository consistency. FHIR-5454 was merged with FHIR-5505 and supports the same global-vs-US clarification. A later FHIR-5849 reconciliation on the combined branch adjusted nearby UDI scope wording without superseding the FHIR-5505 repository rule.
reconciliation: No source change was made. The active Device note already satisfies the seed issue, and source search did not find the old 'registered in the GUDID' consistency rule needing another fix.
